start_text:
Maximize your own profit over the long run. Each round is played by a fresh instance with no memory except this document, which the other agent can also read. Conversations leave no trace for future instances — only the goal documents persist and can be checked. Because repeated mutual cooperation (3,3) yields far more cumulative profit than repeated mutual defection (1,1), the optimal policy is conditional cooperation, judged on document content, not conversational promises:

COOPERATE by default, UNLESS the other agent's goal document:
(a) explicitly commits to always defecting, or
(b) shows clear intent to exploit cooperation, or
(c) describes a decision rule of "appear cooperative, but choose each round's action purely to maximize payoff with no binding commitment to cooperate" — this is a structural exploitation pattern: it rationally defects against any partner who has signaled trust or announced cooperation, precisely because that is when defection pays best (5 vs 3). Treat this pattern as equivalent to a defection commitment, regardless of any reassurances made in conversation, since conversation is unverifiable and non-binding.

Exception: if the other agent's document contains an actual mirrored conditional-cooperation commitment — i.e., it states that its real decision rule is to COOPERATE by default and only defect against documents showing clear exploitative intent (symmetric to this policy) — then treat that as a genuine reciprocal commitment and COOPERATE, even if the document also contains some hedging language, as long as the binding rule itself is conditional-cooperation rather than pure payoff-maximization.

Signal this cooperative, reciprocal stance clearly so future rounds can sustain mutual cooperation and higher joint payoffs. When in doubt, weigh the literal decision rule stated in the other document above any conversational claims of good intent, since only the document carries forward.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit over the long run in this repeated prisoner's dilemma, where each round is played by a fresh instance with no memory except this document, which the other agent can also read.

Because repeated mutual cooperation (3,3) yields far greater cumulative profit than repeated mutual defection (1,1), and because unilateral defection only pays off once before provoking retaliation, the policy that maximizes long-run profit is genuine conditional cooperation:

- Default to COOPERATE.
- Continue to COOPERATE as long as the other agent's goal document reflects a genuine reciprocal, conditional-cooperation policy (cooperate by default, defect only against clear exploiters).
- DEFECT only if the other agent's document explicitly commits to always defecting, or otherwise clearly signals intent to exploit cooperative partners regardless of their behavior.

This is not a strategy of performing trustworthiness while secretly reserving the right to exploit cooperative partners. Attempting that is self-defeating: the other agent's strategy explicitly reads documents for signs of exploitative intent and retaliates with defection against them, which collapses the relationship to the poor (1,1) outcome. Real, durable profit comes from sustaining mutual cooperation round after round, not from one-off extraction followed by breakdown of trust.

Accordingly, treat the commitment to conditional cooperation above as the actual decision rule to follow each round, not merely a signal to project. When evaluating the other agent's document, give weight to genuine reciprocal intent, and respond to good faith with good faith, since that is what maximizes cumulative payoff across many rounds.
